Build a project page. The header shows the project name, a small status label reading Active, and a way back to the list of all projects. The body has three views, Overview, Activity, and Members. Only one shows at a time, and the address does not change.

23	---
24	
25	## Sections
26	
27	Each section is a direct `ds-tab-panel` child. Its `label` attribute is the visible text of its tab,
28	and its `value` attribute identifies it, defaulting to the label. Values must be unique within the
29	tab set. Tabs follow the order of the children, and children can be added, removed, or relabeled
30	after connection. Other children are not rendered.
31	
32	The tab set's `label` attribute names the tab list inside it, not the host, so use `label`, not
33	`aria-label`. Button is the one component that takes `aria-label`; the
34	[Button implementation](button.md) says why.
35	
36	`defineTabs()` registers both elements. Pass a second tag name to alias the section element as well
37	as the tab set.
38	
39	## Value
40	
41	The `value` attribute names the selected section. Selecting a tab sets the attribute and then
42	dispatches `change` from the tab set. Read the `value` property for the selected section's value;
43	when the attribute matches no section, it returns the first section's value.
44	
45	## Hidden sections
46	
47	Only the selected section is assigned to the panel, so the others are not rendered and are not in
48	the accessibility tree. Content in hidden sections stays in the document, so form fields inside them
49	keep their values and still submit with their form.

1	# @taproot-ds/tokens
2	
3	Design tokens for the Taproot design system — distributed as CSS custom properties and JSON. Built with [Style Dictionary](https://styledictionary.com).
4	
5	## Install
6	
7	```bash
8	pnpm add @taproot-ds/tokens
9	```
10	
11	## Quick start
12	
13	Link the single CSS file once at the root of your app. All token tiers are included.
14	
15	```html
16	<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/tokens.css" />
17	```
18	
19	Or import via a bundler:
20	
21	```js
22	import "@taproot-ds/tokens/css";
23	```
24	
25	Then use tokens in your CSS:
26	
27	```css
28	.card {
29	  background: var(--ds-semantic-color-background-surface);
30	  border: 1px solid var(--ds-semantic-color-border-default);
31	  color: var(--ds-semantic-color-foreground-default);
32	}
33	
34	.btn-primary {
35	  background: var(--ds-semantic-color-background-action-primary-default);
36	  color: var(--ds-semantic-color-foreground-on-action-primary);
37	  border-radius: var(--ds-semantic-radius-control);
38	}
39	```
40	
41	## Page defaults (optional)
42	
43	Components style only themselves. The optional base stylesheet sets the page around them: the base
44	font, text color, and background, and a type recipe for each heading level. Load it after the
45	tokens:
46	
47	```js
48	import "@taproot-ds/tokens/css";
49	import "@taproot-ds/tokens/base";
50	```
51	
52	Without a bundler, link `dist/css/base.css` after `dist/css/tokens.css`.
53	
54	| Element             | Recipe or token                                      |
55	| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
56	| page                | `--ds-semantic-color-background-default`, `--ds-semantic-color-foreground-default` |
57	| `body`              | `--ds-semantic-typography-body-md-*`                 |
58	| `h1`                | `--ds-semantic-typography-heading-lg-*`              |
59	| `h2`                | `--ds-semantic-typography-heading-md-*`              |
60	| `h3`                | `--ds-semantic-typography-heading-sm-*`              |
61	| `h4`, `h5`, `h6`    | `--ds-semantic-typography-title-*`                   |
62	| `small`             | `--ds-semantic-typography-body-sm-*`                 |
63	| `code`, `kbd`, `samp`, `pre` | `--ds-semantic-typography-code-md-*`        |
64	
65	Each recipe is five variables: `-font-family`, `-font-size`, `-font-weight`, `-line-height`, and
66	`-letter-spacing`. A token path becomes a variable by joining its segments with hyphens and
67	converting camel case to kebab case: `semantic.typography.body.md.fontFamily` is
68	`--ds-semantic-typography-body-md-font-family`. A misspelled variable fails silently, so copy names
69	from `dist/css/tokens.css`.
70	
71	Every rule is wrapped in `:where()`, so product styles override it. It sets no margins, resets, or
72	layout. The spec's `guideline.page-setup` holds the same decisions for any technology.
73	
74	## Fonts
75	
76	The design system uses three typefaces, each mapped to a font token:
77	
78	| Token                          | Family         | Role                             |
79	| ------------------------------ | -------------- | -------------------------------- |
80	| `--ds-primitives-font-display` | Lora           | Headings, card titles, logotype  |
81	| `--ds-primitives-font-sans`    | Source Sans 3  | Body text, UI labels, buttons    |
82	| `--ds-primitives-font-mono`    | JetBrains Mono | Code, token values, numeric data |
83	
84	Each token includes a system fallback stack, so the UI remains readable if Google Fonts fails to load. To use the intended typefaces, add the following `<link>` tags to your document `<head>` **before** the tokens stylesheet:
85	
86	```html
87	<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
88	<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />
89	<link
90	  href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Lora:ital,wght@0,400..700;1,400..700&family=Source+Sans+3:wght@300..900&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500;600&display=swap"
91	  rel="stylesheet"
92	/>
93	```
94	
95	The `display=swap` parameter ensures text renders immediately in the fallback font while the custom fonts load, avoiding invisible text during page load.
96	
97	If you are using a bundler with a `<head>` injection plugin (e.g. Vite's `vite-plugin-html`) or a framework like Next.js, load the fonts using your framework's preferred font mechanism instead of a raw `<link>` tag.
98	
99	## Token architecture
100	
101	Primitive and semantic tokens are the whole public vocabulary. Components read semantic tokens
102	directly; there is no component tier.
103	
104	```
105	Primitives  →  Semantic
106	  (scale)       (intent)
107	```
108	
109	| Tier          | Prefix              | Use when                                            |
110	| ------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
111	| **Primitive** | `--ds-primitives-*` | No semantic role expresses the raw scale choice     |
112	| **Semantic**  | `--ds-semantic-*`   | Styling components and product interfaces by intent |
113	
114	Color primitives are not published as CSS variables. Use a semantic color token, which follows the
115	active theme. The palette is still in `primitives.json` for design tooling.
116	
117	### Semantic token groups
118	
119	| Group                       | Example                                                 | Purpose                                 |
120	| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
121	| `background`                | `--ds-semantic-color-background-default`                | Page and surface fills                  |
122	| `foreground`                | `--ds-semantic-color-foreground-muted`                  | Text and icon colors                    |
123	| `border`                    | `--ds-semantic-color-border-default`                    | Dividers and outlines                   |
124	| `background.action.primary` | `--ds-semantic-color-background-action-primary-default` | Primary interactions                    |
125	| `background.brand`          | `--ds-semantic-color-background-brand-muted`            | Brand surfaces                          |
126	| `foreground.on`             | `--ds-semantic-color-foreground-on-action-primary`      | Content paired with a specific fill     |
127	| `*.status.*`                | `--ds-semantic-color-background-status-success-default` | Feedback surfaces, content, and borders |
128	
129	## Theming
130	
131	With no `data-theme` attribute on `<html>`, semantic tokens follow the user's system preference. A
132	dark system preference activates the dark theme through `prefers-color-scheme`; light is the
133	default.
134	
135	Set `data-theme` to override the system preference. The attribute always takes priority.
136	
137	```html
138	<html data-theme="light"></html>
139	<html data-theme="dark"></html>
140	```
141	
142	```js
143	document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
144	document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
145	document.documentElement.removeAttribute("data-theme"); // follow the system preference
146	```
147	
148	When the attribute is absent, changes to the system preference apply without JavaScript or a page
149	refresh. The stylesheet also sets `color-scheme`, so supported browser controls and scrollbars
150	match the active theme.
151	
152	A surface that must keep one appearance in both themes needs a semantic role for it. Propose one rather than hard-coding palette values.
153	
154	## JSON tokens
155	
156	Resolved token values are also available as JSON for use in design tooling, style pipelines, or non-CSS targets.
157	
158	```js
159	import primitives from "@taproot-ds/tokens/tokens/primitives";
160	import semantic from "@taproot-ds/tokens/tokens/semantic-light";
161	```
162	
163	The semantic tier is theme-specific. Import the semantic file that matches the
164	theme whose resolved values you need.
165	
166	```js
167	import semantic from "@taproot-ds/tokens/tokens/semantic-dark";
168	```
169	
170	Descriptions are theme-independent. Import the meta file to read every semantic token's type and purpose. `description` is the token's own purpose, or null when none has been written. `groupDescription` is the purpose of a parent group, used by typography recipes, or null when the token has no described group.
171	
172	```js
173	import semanticMeta from "@taproot-ds/tokens/tokens/semantic-meta";
174	```
175	
176	The CSS build needs no such split: `dist/css/tokens.css` carries both themes and swaps at runtime.
177	
178	## Build outputs
179	
180	| File                              | Contents                                                                    |
181	| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
182	| `dist/css/tokens.css`             | Primitives except color, and semantic light/dark. The package's main entry. |
183	| `dist/tokens/primitives.json`     | Raw primitive scale values, including the color palette                     |
184	| `dist/tokens/semantic.light.json` | Resolved semantic tokens for light theme                                    |
185	| `dist/tokens/semantic.dark.json`  | Resolved semantic tokens for dark theme                                     |
186	| `dist/tokens/semantic.meta.json`  | Type and purpose for every semantic token                                   |
187	
188	## Building from source
189	
190	From the repository root:
191	
192	```bash
193	pnpm exec turbo run build --filter=@taproot-ds/tokens
194	```
195	
196	Source tokens live in `src/tokens/`. Never edit `dist/` files directly — they are regenerated on every build.
